callModel.description: Explicit call collection and binding model. js-ts-lexical-v1 collects CallExpressions from parse-valid non-declaration JS/TS files and binds declarations, direct const initializers and relative named imports to direct exports. js-ts-lexical-v2 additionally binds relative default imports to direct default function declarations with one implementation body. Absent or unrecognized models do not establish call coverage; adapterRevision alone is insufficient.

root.description: Analyzed directory, relative to the Git repository root ("." when equal).

baseRevision.description: Contextual HEAD only, not the revision of the analyzed working-tree contents.

snapshotId.description: Digest identifying the extracted facts and captured source text.

url.description: Git origin URL as configured; null when there is no Git repository or no origin.

adapter.description: Parser or runtime the adapter used, with its version.

adapterRevision.description: Revision of the adapter's own extraction logic. Absent in facts written before revisions were recorded.

sourceText.description: Exact text parsed by the extractor, retained for consistent source navigation.

imports.description: Recorded source dependencies. Java also records type references that may denote an analyzed type; static describes a statically recorded edge, not specifically Java's import static keyword.

to.description: Present only when resolved inside the analyzed tree.

lazy.description: Import occurs in a deferred body. Its caller may still run during module initialization; this is not a safety guarantee.

typeOnly.description: Type-only dependency, excluded from runtime import-cycle analysis.

conditional.description: Execution depends on a guard, exception, or loop not evaluated by the analyzer.

implicit.description: Python package initializer loaded by this import; line points to the initiating statement.

functions.description: Function-level measurements from Python, JS/TS or Java. Absent when the adapter does not measure functions, which the complexity rule treats as not checked rather than clean.

complexity.description: Cyclomatic complexity: 1 plus each branch point (see extract/py/extract.py).

nesting.description: Deepest block nesting inside the body; elif stays at its if's depth.

symbols.description: Module-scope bindings per file (Python adapter): the line where a name becomes bound at import time. Used to identify potential partial-initialization risks in import cycles; static binding order does not prove runtime failure. Empty for adapters that do not emit them.

calls.description: TS/JS CallExpression sites in syntactically valid non-declaration files. Same-file-function means lexical binding to one body-bearing ordinary function declaration, not runtime dispatch, execution or reachability. same-file-function-initializer for a unique const identifier variable directly initialized with an arrow/function expression. imported-function for relative static imports resolved to captured direct exports: named function/const-initializer exports in v1, plus default function declarations in v2; target.file is relative to the analysis root. Empty arrays from older/other adapters remain valid; see callModel and parse_errors for coverage.

endLine.description: One-based end-exclusive CallExpression end line (TypeScript getEnd).

name.description: Measured function name; a named function expression uses its inner name, which may differ from the const variable name.

column.description: 1-based UTF-16 column at the function declaration or initializer expression start in target.file for imported-function, otherwise the callsite file (including modifiers).

packageMarkers.description: Package marker files (package.json, pyproject.toml, __init__.py; for Java also pom.xml, build.gradle, build.gradle.kts) under the analyzed root, relative POSIX paths. Module grouping uses them as package boundaries; adapters do not parse them.

parse_errors.description: Files the adapter could not parse; they keep their file record but contribute no imports.

external.description: Third-party or standard-library dependencies: bare or node: specifiers, Python modules outside the tree, Java imports of packages no analyzed file declares.

outside.description: Resolved to a file outside the analyzed root.

unknown.description: Dependencies that look internal but could not be resolved: path-like or in-tree specifiers, Java names in an analyzed package or matching an analyzed type.

opaque.description: Dynamic import/require whose specifier is not a string literal (recorded as "<computed>").
